deployment.describes: the production deployment that was live when this build was generated (resolved from the Vercel CLI at build time). This is NOT the deployment that serves these bytes: a static file cannot carry the id of the deployment that uploads it, and the serving deployment is exactly one newer. Read `derivable:false` + `previous:true` as that statement, and check the id against Vercel's deployment list. /data/versions.json.live carries the same id and the same labels.
deployment.note: derived, not typed: resolved with `vercel inspect <domain> --json` at build time. A stale id pretending to be the serving deployment is a provenance defect; an explicitly-labelled previous id is not.

serving_deployment.reason: a static file cannot contain the id of the deployment that uploads it; the id named in this block is the deployment that was live when the build ran, and this build supersedes it. Ask Vercel's deployment list (or `vercel inspect the95xrecord.vercel.app`) which deployment is serving now — that answer is authoritative, this file is not.
